newsitem.title: HAITI: One wounded as Haitian police, demonstrators clash.
newsitem.headline: One wounded as Haitian police, demonstrators clash.

text.p: One man lost his hand and several other people were injured on Thursday in a tear gas blast when a special unit of the Haitian police quashed an anti-government demonstration, sparking panic and a stampede by the crowd.

Witnesses said about 300 demonstrators who were calling for Prime Minister Rosny Smarth to step down, were peacefully singing in front of the National Palace when some 25 members of the rapid response police unit, dressed in full riot gear, arrived and began firing tear gas bombs.
The bombs were a combination gas and concussion grenade designed to make noise as well as disperse gas, a U.S. Embassy official said.

The demonstrators represented 70 popular organisations frustrated with a lack of improvement in the quality of life in Haiti, the poorest nation in the hemisphere. They recently promised to march every day to voice their opposition to Smarth and other government ministers.

More than two years since a force of some 20,000 U.S.-led international troops restored its freely-elected government, Haiti continues to struggle with 80 percent unemployment, widespread illiteracy and a lack of basic services such as potable drinking water and electricity.
Demonstrators also expressed scepticism of the government's plans, backed by international lenders, to privatise state industries including the power and telephone companies.

"We want Rosny Smarth to go because he doesn't listen to the people," said demonstrator Britto Joel. "The government is listening to the international community. We voted for President Rene Preval, but not for Smarth."
The explosions heard after police arrived sent the demonstrators running, trampling anyone in their way.
Dieuseul Sibil, 23, lost his hand either to a shotgun blast or after being hit by a tear gas bomb. The former telephone company employee said police fired a grenade at him.
"The rapid response unit did this to me," he told Reuters from his hospital bed. "My hand was blown off because I was criticising the government."

Police spokesman Felder Jean-Baptiste said the man had picked up a gas grenade fired into the crowd and attempted to throw it back at police when it exploded. Witnesses said a shotgun had blown Sibil's hand off and police themselves questioned whether a gas bomb could have done such damage.
The demonstrators threw rocks and beat on cars in the chaos, especially after finding bits of Sibil's hand scattered in the street.
"Now we know whose side this government is on," said one angry man. "We are going to burn tires and destroy houses."
